claims.text: A tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy containing low-activation refractory elements can serve as a low-activation structural material for high-temperature plasma-facing components in fusion reactors.
Conventional tungsten and tungsten alloys have high melting points.
Conventional tungsten or tungsten alloys suffer from embrittlement.
Conventional tungsten or tungsten alloys have problematic activation under neutron irradiation.
Alloying tungsten with low-activation refractory elements can induce a complex, stabilized microstructure.
The proposed alloying strategy can mitigate radiation-induced damage.
Fusion-reactor plasma-facing regions can expose structural materials to temperatures exceeding 1000 °C and high neutron fluxes.
A multi-principal-element microstructure promotes lattice distortion and phase stability.
Lattice distortion and phase stability retard irradiation-defect migration and agglomeration.
Introducing additional low-activation refractory elements into tungsten in a high-entropy design lowers irradiation-defect formation.
Introducing additional low-activation refractory elements into tungsten in a high-entropy design lowers irradiation-defect mobility.
The proposed tungsten-based HEA maintains structural integrity at high temperatures.
The proposed tungsten-based HEA has reduced long-term activation relative to conventional alloys.
The tungsten-based refractory HEA will have better high-temperature mechanical performance than conventional tungsten alloys or reduced-activation steels.
The tungsten-based refractory HEA will resist irradiation-induced embrittlement better than conventional tungsten alloys or reduced-activation steels.
The tungsten-based refractory HEA will produce lower levels of long-lived radioactive isotopes than conventional tungsten alloys or reduced-activation steels.
EUROFER is a reduced-activation ferritic/martensitic steel considered for fusion structural applications.
Unforeseen phases arising from the selected alloying elements could limit the proposed benefits.
Alloying elements with unfavorable activation under fusion-neutron spectra could limit the proposed reduction in activation.
Processing route and microstructural control are critical to realizing the proposed material performance.
